title: Quantum Circuit and Tensor Network Implementation of the 2D Acoustic Wave Equation
abstract: We present a cohesive framework for simulating seismic wave propagation utilizing quantum computing paradigms and their classical tensor network equivalents.   We detail a quantum circuit-based formulation for the explicit finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solution of the two-dimensional acoustic wave equation and   map this quantum architecture onto a tensor train representation, namely for Matrix Product State (MPS).   The MPS solver enables deterministic simulation of large-scale wavefield dynamics on classical high-performance computing systems.   We demonstrate the MPS representation by computing 2D seismic wavefields on the Marmousi model.   Our results indicate that the MPS representation is a viable direction for computing and scaling wavefield propagation.
summary: This work develops a framework to simulate seismic wave propagation by translating the acoustic wave equation into a quantum circuit model. Crucially, they show how this quantum evolution can be deterministically emulated on classical hardware using Matrix Product States (MPS) via Tensor Network techniques. This establishes MPS as a scalable and viable computational tool for large-scale wavefield dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating seismic wave propagation governed by the 2D acoustic wave equation in complex media.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that mapping the wavefield dynamics onto a Tensor Train/Matrix Product State (MPS) representation provides a viable, deterministic classical emulation bridge for simulating large-scale wavefield propagation.
method: The simulation uses an explicit Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) formulation, which is then mapped onto a quantum circuit model and subsequently emulated classically using Matrix Product Operators (MPOs) within the Tensor Network framework.
model_or_system: The physical system is the 2D acoustic wavefield u(x, z, t) governed by the wave equation, simulated using the Marmousi model as a test case.
key_observables: The resulting 2D seismic wavefields generated by the simulation.
important_parameters: The bond dimension $\chi$ in the MPS representation, the time step $\Delta t$, and the CFL stability criterion.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the MPS representation can accurately emulate the quantum evolution, requiring periodic truncation via SVD to maintain computational tractability.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares the 2D seismic wavefields generated by both the standard FDTD solver and the MPS solver for the Marmousi model.
paper_structure: The paper details the quantum circuit formulation for the FDTD update, maps this to a Tensor Train/MPS representation using MPOs, and validates the MPS solver by comparing its results against the established FDTD solver.
why_interesting: While the core physics is seismology, the methodology—translating a continuous PDE evolution into a structured tensor network update—is highly relevant for simulating complex dynamics in quantum many-body systems where exact diagonalization is impossible.
